Package fr.sorbonne_u.devs_simulation.models

DEVS models.

See: Description

  • Class Summary 
    Class Description
    AbstractAtomicModelFactory
    The abstract class AbstractAtomicModelFactory provides the basic implementation for atomic model factories.
    AbstractCoupledModelFactory
    The abstract class AbstractCoupledModelFactory provides the basic implementation for coupled model factories.
    AtomicModel
    The class AtomicModel implements the most general methods and instance variables for DEVS atomic models.
    AtomicModel.Destination
    The class Destination gathers information about the destination for the exchange of external events.
    CoupledModel
    The class CoupledModel implements the most general methods and instance variables for DEVS coupled models.
    Model
    The class Model is the root of the class hierarchy implementing variants of DEVS simulation models for a component plug-in implementing a family of DEVS simulation engines.
    StandardAtomicModelFactory
    The class StandardAtomicModelFactory defines an atomic model factory that will create models from their Java representation class, assuming that this model class declares a constructor with the three standard parameters: the URI of the model, the simulation time unit and the simulation engine.
    StandardCoupledModelFactory
    The class StandardCoupledModelFactory defines a coupled model factory that will create models from their Java representation class, assuming that this model class declares a constructor with the standard parameters as they appear in the constructor of the class CoupledModel.
    StandardRTAtomicModelFactory
    The class StandardRTAtomicModelFactory implements the standard model factory for real time atomic models.
    StandardRTCoupledModelFactory
    The class StandardRTCoupledModelFactory implements a standard model factory for real time coupled models.

This package defines the interfaces and abstract classes implementing the core behaviour of DEVS models. It also defines the factories used in simulation architecture descriptions to instantiate models when required. Models that obey the standard instantiation protocols (constructors with the same parameters) defined by the classes in this package do not need to use factories. The composition process can use model classes directly for instantiation rather than factories in this case.
